title: SpaceX Is About to Become the Biggest IPO in History. Here Is What Every NRI Investor Needs to Know.
excerpt: Elon Musk's rocket-and-AI company lists on Nasdaq June 12 at a $1.77 trillion valuation, with 30 per cent of shares reserved for retail investors. For NRIs with US brokerage accounts, the window is narrow and the stakes are enormous.
body:
On Thursday, June 12, SpaceX will begin trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX. The IPO price is set at $135 per share. The company is selling 555.6 million shares to raise $75 billion, valuing the entire enterprise at $1.77 trillion.

That makes it the largest initial public offering in history, by a wide margin.

For the Indian diaspora in America — a community with one of the highest rates of retail brokerage participation in the country — the listing is both an opportunity and a test of discipline. The numbers are staggering. The risks are real. And the window to decide is roughly 48 hours.

## The Three Businesses Inside SpaceX

SpaceX is not just a rocket company. Since its merger with xAI, Elon Musk's artificial intelligence venture, the company now has three distinct segments that investors are buying into.

**Rocket launch** remains the most iconic business. SpaceX has launched roughly 650 Falcon rockets with a 99 per cent success rate and pioneered reusable boosters that fundamentally changed the economics of reaching orbit. This segment is profitable and dominant — no competitor comes close.

**Starlink**, the satellite internet division, operates approximately 9,600 satellites in low-Earth orbit, delivering broadband to millions of customers in 164 countries. It is the largest satellite constellation ever built and generates meaningful revenue, particularly in underserved markets including rural India.

**Artificial intelligence** is where the valuation gets controversial. The AI division, powered by the xAI merger and the Grok AI platform, generated just $3.2 billion in revenue last year with negative net profits. SpaceX has plans to build and launch solar-powered orbital data centres and has already secured massive compute deals — $920 million per month from Alphabet through June 2029, and $1.25 billion per month from Anthropic. Morgan Stanley projects the AI division could drive SpaceX revenues to $3.4 trillion by 2040. Goldman Sachs forecasts AI revenue hitting $322 billion by 2030. Both banks are underwriters for the IPO.

## The Bull and Bear Cases

The bull case writes itself: Musk has built the most successful rocket company in history, the most valuable satellite network ever deployed, and is now positioning to dominate space-based AI infrastructure. MSCI has confirmed SpaceX will be fast-tracked into its Global Standard Indexes, meaning passively managed funds with $5.79 trillion in assets will be forced to buy shares. The Nasdaq 100 and FTSE Russell indexes are also clearing the way. When index inclusion happens, typically 10 trading days after listing, a wall of institutional money will flow in regardless of the price.

The bear case is equally real. SpaceX posted a net loss of $4.94 billion in 2025, despite 33 per cent revenue growth to $18.67 billion. At the IPO price, the company trades at 94.5 times its 2025 sales — Tesla, by comparison, trades at 16.7 times. Morningstar has pegged a fair value estimate at $780 billion, less than half the listing target. University of Florida data tracking nearly 9,300 IPOs from 1980 to 2024 shows that investors who buy on the first day of trading and hold for three years see returns roughly 21 per cent lower than a simple S&P 500 index fund.

Only about 7 per cent of SpaceX's listed shares will be freely tradeable at launch, which means low float, high volatility, and prices that could swing wildly in either direction.

## The Retail Investor Angle

What makes this IPO unusual is the retail allocation. SpaceX is reserving up to 30 per cent of the offering for individual investors — about $22.5 billion worth of shares. The standard allocation is 5 to 10 per cent. Retail investors can participate through banks including Bank of America, Citigroup, and Morgan Stanley, as well as through some online brokerages. E*TRADE has set account balance and risk tolerance thresholds, though exact figures have not been publicly disclosed.

For NRIs with US brokerage accounts, this represents direct access to what could be the defining IPO of the decade. For those investing through Indian platforms, access may be available through global investment channels such as Mizuho Securities in Asia and UBS in Europe, though regulatory constraints and minimum thresholds apply.

## The Inflation Backdrop

The SpaceX IPO lands in a treacherous macro environment. The May Consumer Price Index, due out Wednesday — the day before trading begins — is expected to show headline inflation at 4.2 per cent year-over-year, the highest since May 2023. Core inflation is projected at 2.9 per cent. The Iran war has pushed oil above $90 per barrel and rattled supply chains. Bond markets are pricing in a possible Fed rate hike before year-end. Small business sentiment has fallen to its lowest level since 2019.

For NRI investors juggling portfolios across two countries, this context matters. Higher US interest rates strengthen the dollar, which is good for remittances but bad for Indian equity valuations. The Nifty 50 is trading near a two-month low of 23,123, with seven straight sessions of foreign investor selling. Wipro just announced a Rs 15,000 crore buyback at Rs 250 per share, a move widely read as a floor-setting exercise after the stock hit a three-year low.

## What NRIs Should Actually Do

The honest answer is that nobody knows whether SpaceX at $135 is a bargain or a trap. What the data shows is this: mega-IPOs historically underperform in the short term, index inclusion creates a structural tailwind in the medium term, and the AI business that justifies most of the valuation is still unprofitable and unproven at scale.

If you have a US brokerage account and want exposure, know that the final IPO price is set June 11. If you are investing from India, check whether your platform offers international IPO access and be aware of the RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme limits.

The biggest IPO in history starts trading in three days. The clock is running.

**Sources:** Reuters, Investopedia, Morningstar, MSCI, New York Post, The Motley Fool
